section: USA elements | for tall units H. 210
source_pages: printed p.418 / PDF 420 (extracted whole: both types)
family_naming_note: Namespaced 'USA Tall H.210' for the same reason as 'Wall H.36': the registry merges section files by family NAME, and 'H.210' also names a metric tall family in the Maxima chapter (printed p.111-131) which is a different thing. The catalog's own wording is preserved in 'section'. This is the registry's first TALL-class family and its first USA elements row.
extraction_note: printed p.418 taken whole - four widths x two types, eight codes. This page was chosen as the first USA extraction over printed p.414 for one reason: p.414's four types are ALL custom-sized ('1 custom-sized fixed front', '1 custom-sized jumbo drawer'), and the Object Contract cannot yet say that a front's width comes from the opening rather than from the code. p.418 states plain fixed widths, so it extracts honestly today.
inch_note: THIS IS THE PAGE THAT PRINTS INCHES. It carries an inch column to the LEFT of the centimetre column - 18" 45.7, 24" 61, 30" 76.2, 36" 91.4 - the only place in the 634-page book that states an inch size at all. The nominal is resolved from the width by _manifest.json nominal_widths_in, which is why no nominal field appears on the rows here: a lookup, never arithmetic, and never duplicated.

usa_fridge_door.notes: A PANEL, not a cabinet - it faces the client's own fridge, the same relationship the dishwasher door has to its machine on printed p.47. depth_mm is the front thickness (22, the UCON standard), not a carcass depth. HANDED IS FALSE, AND NOT FOR WANT OF INFORMATION. The description reads '1 door' and not '1 rh or lh door', which is the wording every handed unit in this catalog uses - and the difference is real, not an omission. THE TWO MARKETS INTEGRATE A FRIDGE DIFFERENTLY (explained by Andriy 2026-08-21). In Europe the appliance is built INSIDE a cabinet: the cabinet carries the hinges and its own door is linked to the appliance door by a sliding bracket, so the hand is a property of the CABINET and the factory must be told it. In America the fridge stands in a housing BETWEEN two neighbouring cabinets, or between panels, and the panel is mounted DIRECTLY on the appliance. The hand is then the appliance's business, not the cabinetry's, and the factory has no part in it. So '1 door' is the complete and correct description of this article. Do NOT add hinge_side to it and do NOT ask an estimate about it. No swing symbol is drawn, and here that is the right answer rather than a deferral.

front_layout.note: One full-height panel, 2100 tall. No hinge_axis: this is not a hung door, and the vertical hinge it must really have is not stated by the source - see notes. Nothing is drawn rather than something wrong.

usa_wine_cooler_door.description: Door for USA fridge - 1 wine cooler door
usa_wine_cooler_door.notes: Same four widths as the plain fridge door, one suffix apart (00 -> 01). Carries a cutout on the front, so it is not simply the other door in a different finish. The page prints two restrictions that are NOT modelled and must not be lost: (1) a surcharge of 234 points for the stainless steel protection for the wine cooler door, with NO article code - recorded here, never invented as a companion, the same treatment Servo Drive gets on the wall pages; (2) a prohibition mark against 'Maxima 2.2 with framed door' and 'Metal doors', and a positive instruction to use melamine, Technomat, Unicolor or Fenix. Finish is a composition-level axis the engine does not model at all yet (M1.6), so this restriction has nowhere to live but this note.

front_layout.note: One full-height panel, 2100 tall, with a cutout the catalog does not dimension. Envelope-only: the cutout is recorded in notes and not drawn. No hinge_axis, for the same reason as the plain fridge door.
